statement: A pool care guide says the pH of the water, $p$, should be at least $6.2$ and at most $7.8$. Which of the following inequalities describes exactly the recommended values of $p$?

choices.misconception: I used the midpoint $7$ correctly but used the whole width of the range, $7.8 - 6.2 = 1.6$, as the allowed distance instead of half of it.
I started from the lowest allowed value, $6.2$, and used the full width $1.6$, but the number inside the absolute value has to be the center of the range.
I found the midpoint $7$ and the half-width $0.8$, but I put them in each other's places in the inequality.

hints: $|p - c| \le d$ means $p$ is within $d$ of $c$.
Find the midpoint of $6.2$ and $7.8$, and how far each end is from that midpoint.
The midpoint is $7$, and each end is $0.8$ away from it.

solutions.reliable: The inequality $|p - c| \le d$ means $c - d \le p \le c + d$. We need $c - d = 6.2$ and $c + d = 7.8$. Adding these gives $2c = 14$, so $c = 7$, and then $d = 0.8$. The inequality is $|p - 7| \le 0.8$. Check: it allows exactly $6.2 \le p \le 7.8$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
